readers.reasoning: Struct members and subarrays of pointer members may appear in data clauses; copyin(r) then copyin(r.nx[0:2]) and r.nx[0][0:1] attach pointers in present device data, and the exit data deletes run in child-before-parent order, so counters reach zero cleanly. The subarray applies to the array element r.nx[0], not to a struct subarray, so the 'members of a subarray' ban does not apply (small ambiguity). The delete clause defines detach and deallocate actions for exactly this; a hang from an unhandled delete kind is a runtime defect, not a permitted outcome.

Struct r copied in, then member sections attached via nested enter data; deletes mirror the enters with dynamic reference counts of one. Present(r) holds. Nothing nonconforming; the hang/unhandled kind is a runtime defect.

r is copied in, then r.nx[0:2] and r.nx[0][0:1] are copied in with attach of r.nx and r.nx[0]; exit data deletes happen in reverse order. Each delete decrements the attachment counter, detaches at zero, and decrements the dynamic count; any extra decrement leaves the counter at zero. The serial region only uses r.v. All well defined, so a conforming implementation must run it without hanging.

Whole struct r is copied in, then r.nx[0:2] and the subarray r.nx[0][0:1] are copied in, which attach the pointer members in turn. Members and subarrays of members may appear in data clauses. Exit deletes in reverse order, so no pointer is detached from freed data. The serial region uses only r.v. The program is conforming and must run with tot=6; the libgomp UNHANDLED kind and hang are an implementation defect.

Struct members and subarrays of members may appear in data clauses; r.nx[0:2] uses subarray notation on a member whose parent r is not a subarray, and r.nx[0][0:1] selects no member of a subarray. The program appears conforming, and a hang with an unhandled map kind in the runtime is a compiler or runtime defect, but attach/detach of nested pointers is not spelled out fully enough to be sure.
